findings.title: Privileged container
findings.remediation: Remove securityContext.privileged; grant only the specific capability required.

findings.title: Host namespaces shared
findings.remediation: Remove hostNetwork/hostPID/hostIPC unless this is a node agent that truly needs it.
stackroxPolicies: Docker CIS 5.9 and 5.20: Ensure that the host's network namespace is not shared
Docker CIS 5.15: Ensure that the host's process namespace is not shared
Docker CIS 5.16: Ensure that the host's IPC namespace is not shared

findings.title: Container may run as root
findings.remediation: Set runAsNonRoot: true (pod or container securityContext) and build images with a non-root USER.
stackroxPolicies: Docker CIS 4.1: Ensure That a User for the Container Has Been Created

findings.title: Namespace has workloads but no NetworkPolicy
findings.message: No NetworkPolicy for namespace bench in this bundle.
findings.remediation: Add a default-deny ingress NetworkPolicy plus explicit allows (router/ingress controller, monitoring, same-app traffic).
stackroxPolicies: Deployments should have at least one ingress Network Policy

findings.title: Single replica
findings.remediation: Run at least 2 replicas (3 across zones for production) with a PodDisruptionBudget.

citations.title: Specifying a Disruption Budget for your Application

findings.title: No readiness probe
findings.remediation: Add a readinessProbe (httpGet on a /ready endpoint, or tcpSocket) so traffic only reaches ready pods.

citations.title: Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes

findings.title: Missing CPU/memory requests
findings.remediation: Set resources.requests.cpu and resources.requests.memory from observed usage (p95).

citations.title: Resource Management for Pods and Containers

stackroxPolicies: No CPU request or memory limit specified

findings.title: Missing memory limit

citations.title: Resource Management for Pods and Containers

stackroxPolicies: No CPU request or memory limit specified

findings.title: Mutable image reference
findings.remediation: Pin an explicit version tag, ideally an immutable digest (image@sha256:...).

findings.title: Seccomp profile not set to RuntimeDefault
findings.message: Container 'web' has no RuntimeDefault seccomp profile.
findings.remediation: Set securityContext.seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault at pod level.

citations.title: Kubernetes CVE feed: CVE-2023-2431 bypass of seccomp profile enforcement (empty localhostProfile)

stackroxPolicies: Docker CIS 5.21: Ensure the default seccomp profile is not disabled

findings.title: ServiceAccount token automounted
findings.message: Pod automounts the token of ServiceAccount 'default'.
findings.remediation: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false on the pod (or ServiceAccount) unless the app calls the API.

citations.title: Role Based Access Control Good Practices

stackroxPolicies: Pod Service Account Token Automatically Mounted

findings.title: No liveness probe
findings.remediation: Add a livenessProbe that checks the process itself (not its dependencies); use a startupProbe for slow starts.

citations.title: Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes

findings.title: Privilege escalation not disabled
findings.message: Container 'web' does not set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false.
findings.remediation: Set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false on every container.

findings.title: Capabilities not dropped
findings.message: Container 'web' does not drop ALL capabilities.

findings.title: Writable root filesystem
findings.message: Container 'web' has a writable root filesystem.
findings.remediation: Set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and mount emptyDir volumes for paths the app writes (e.g. /tmp).

controlSummary.note: Findings are evidence about these controls; an assessment decides whether a control is met. A rule under `notEvaluated` had nothing to decide on: `rulesNotEvaluated` says why for each, and a kind that is not in the input is not a kind that is clean.

redTeam.question: What happens if a worker node crashes mid-operation?
evidence: KN-C001 Deployment/bench/bench-web spec.template.spec.containers[0]: Container 'web' has no readinessProbe.
KN-C007 Deployment/bench/bench-web spec.replicas: Deployment runs 1 replica(s).
redTeam.blastRadius: Single-replica or co-located workloads go down until rescheduled (~5 min default eviction for unreachable nodes); RWO volumes stay attached to the dead node and block replacement pods (Multi-Attach) until the attachment times out.
safeguards: replicas >= 2 (3 for production) with topologySpreadConstraints across zones and hostnames
PodDisruptionBudget maxUnavailable: 1
StatefulSet + volumeClaimTemplates (or RWX storage) instead of a shared RWO claim
readinessProbe so traffic shifts only to healthy replicas
verification: oc get pods -o wide -l <app-label>   # replicas on distinct nodes/zones

redTeam.question: What happens if an entire availability zone fails?
redTeam.blastRadius: Replicas concentrated in one zone all fail together; zonal block volumes cannot follow pods to another zone.
safeguards: topologySpreadConstraints on topology.kubernetes.io/zone with maxSkew: 1
StorageClass volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
application-level replication for stateful services (do not rely on a single zonal volume)

redTeam.question: Is there an exposed route, insecure ingress path or open lateral-movement path?
evidence: KN-N001 Deployment/bench/bench-web metadata: No NetworkPolicy for namespace bench in this bundle.
redTeam.blastRadius: Plain-HTTP routes leak credentials; public load balancers and NodePorts expose services to the internet; missing NetworkPolicies let any compromised pod reach this workload.
safeguards: Route tls.termination edge/reencrypt with insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy: Redirect
default-deny NetworkPolicy + allow from the ingress router namespace only
internal load balancers / loadBalancerSourceRanges
verification: curl -sv http://<route-host>/   # must redirect to https

redTeam.question: If an attacker gets code execution in this pod, can they escalate to the node or the cluster?
evidence: KN-S003 Deployment/bench/bench-web spec.template.spec.containers[0].securityContext.runAsUser: Container 'web' runs as UID 0.
KN-S009 Deployment/bench/bench-web spec.template.spec.hostNetwork: Pod sets hostNetwork: true.
not evaluated, so this scenario cannot be called mitigated: KN-S038, KN-S039
redTeam.blastRadius: Privileged containers, host namespaces/paths, dangerous capabilities and broad RBAC each turn a single compromised pod into node or cluster takeover.
safeguards: Pod Security 'restricted' (restricted-v2 SCC on OpenShift)
automountServiceAccountToken: false; least-privilege Roles without wildcards
RHACS/StackRox deploy-time enforcement of the matching default policies

redTeam.question: Can secrets leak through manifests, Git history, env dumps or mounted tokens?
evidence: KN-S014 Deployment/bench/bench-web spec.template.spec: Pod automounts the token of ServiceAccount 'default'.
redTeam.blastRadius: Literal credentials end up in Git, CI logs and `oc get -o yaml`; mounted SA tokens give API access to any attacker with RCE.
safeguards: secretKeyRef / external secret store
automountServiceAccountToken: false
rotate any credential that was ever committed

redTeam.question: Can a traffic spike or memory leak take down neighbours or trigger restart storms?
evidence: KN-C004 Deployment/bench/bench-web spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources: Container 'web' has no cpu/memory request.
KN-C005 Deployment/bench/bench-web spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources: Container 'web' has no memory limit.
redTeam.blastRadius: Unbounded memory triggers node OOM kills of unrelated pods; BestEffort pods are evicted first; aggressive liveness probes amplify slowness into restarts; a manifest that sets spec.replicas under an HPA scales the workload back down on every apply, peak or not.
safeguards: requests + memory limits on every container
namespace LimitRange and ResourceQuota
liveness checks only the process; failureThreshold >= 3
no spec.replicas on a workload an HPA scales; minReplicas sets the floor

redTeam.question: Could a different (malicious or broken) image run than the one that was reviewed?
evidence: KN-S012 Deployment/bench/bench-web spec.template.spec.containers[0].image: Container 'web' uses mutable image 'docker.io/library/nginx:latest'.
redTeam.blastRadius: Mutable tags can be re-pushed; rollbacks become non-deterministic and scans/signatures no longer apply to what runs.
safeguards: pin images by digest
verify signatures (sigstore/cosign) via admission policy
RHACS 'Latest tag' and image-signature policies in enforce mode
